steps.page: How each kind of notice should behave
steps.intro: Seven decisions, one per kind of notice. Each card shows a real one; pick where that kind shows and when it leaves.

steps.headline: Your message was held back: where should it show, and when should it leave?
steps.today: 13 notices, such as "Claude Code is waiting on something — answer it first.". They float over every chat and are meant to leave after 3 to 8 seconds.
steps.problem: Your message is still waiting in the box after the notice leaves, or the notice gets stuck and follows you to other chats.
steps.proposal: Show it only in that chat, and keep it until the reason is gone or you send.

options.label: Strip, until fixed
options.caption: The strip above the message box, as the app shows "Connecting tools…" today.
options.summary: A strip above that chat's message box. It leaves the moment the reason is gone (question answered, reconnected, chat ready) or you send.
pros: Sits right above the message it is about.
Never covers the chat.
Never leaves while your message is still held back.
cons: Pushes the chat up by one line while it shows.

options.label: Floating, until fixed
options.caption: Floating above the message box, as every notice shows today.
options.summary: Floating as today, but only in that chat, and staying until the reason is gone or you send.
pros: Looks like today.
cons: Covers the bottom of the chat for as long as it stays.

options.label: In the chat
options.caption: In the chat, as the app shows an error from the AI service today.
options.summary: A line in the chat, under the last message, until the reason is gone.
pros: Sits beside the question it points to.
cons: Scrolls away as the chat grows.
For a pop-up only on the terminal screen, there is nothing in the chat to sit beside.

steps.checked: Counted and read from the app code on 2026-11-23; every notice is listed under "Every notice, by kind".
steps.caption: A real one, in the app today.

steps.headline: Not sure it went through: where should it show, and when should it leave?
steps.today: 20 notices, such as "YouCoded couldn't confirm your message was sent — check the conversation before sending it again.". They float for 3 to 6 seconds.
steps.problem: They ask you to check something, then vanish before you have checked it, and don't say which message they meant.
steps.proposal: Put the doubt on the message or action it is about, and keep it until the app confirms or you dismiss it.

options.label: On the message
options.caption: A row on the message itself, as the app shows a message that may not have arrived today.
options.summary: Marked on the message or action itself in that chat. Leaves on its own once confirmed, or when you press Dismiss.
pros: You can see exactly which message is in doubt.
The app already does this for one case.
cons: Needs a matching mark for Stop, /clear and model switches, not only messages.

options.label: Strip, until dismissed
options.caption: The strip above the message box, as the app shows "Connecting tools…" today.
options.summary: A strip above that chat's box until confirmed or dismissed.
pros: Hard to miss.
cons: Doesn't point at which message is in doubt.

options.label: Floating, timed
options.caption: Floating above the message box, as every notice shows today.
options.summary: As today, with the timer fixed.
pros: No change to learn.
cons: Gone before you have checked.

steps.checked: Counted and read from the app code on 2026-11-23; every notice is listed under "Every notice, by kind".
steps.caption: A real one, in the app today.

steps.headline: That can't be done here or now: where should it show, and when should it leave?
steps.today: 16 notices, such as "/doctor isn't available in YouCoded-runtime sessions yet.". They float for 3 seconds.
steps.problem: Some are long, and 3 seconds is not enough to read them. They are the direct answer to what you just did.
steps.proposal: Show it in that chat, and keep it until your next action: typing, sending, or switching chats.

options.label: Strip, until you act
options.caption: The strip above the message box, as the app shows "Connecting tools…" today.
options.summary: A strip above that chat's box. Leaves when you type, send, or switch chats.
pros: As long as you need to read it.
Clears itself the moment you move on.
cons: Pushes the chat up by one line.

options.label: Floating, until you act
options.caption: Floating above the message box, as every notice shows today.
options.summary: Floating, only in that chat, until you type, send, or switch chats.
pros: Looks like today.
cons: Covers the bottom of the chat while it stays.

options.label: Floating, timed
options.caption: Floating above the message box, as every notice shows today.
options.summary: As today, with the timer fixed and a longer time for long notices.
pros: Smallest change.
cons: A long notice can still vanish mid-sentence.

steps.checked: Counted and read from the app code on 2026-11-23; every notice is listed under "Every notice, by kind".
steps.caption: A real one, in the app today.

steps.headline: Something in this chat failed: where should it show, and when should it leave?
steps.today: 20 notices, such as "The model couldn’t write a usable summary, so the conversation was left intact. Try again later.". They float for 3 to 8 seconds.
steps.problem: A failure in a chat vanishes, leaving no record in that chat of what went wrong.
steps.proposal: Put it in the chat where it happened, like an AI service error, and keep it until your next message or until you dismiss it.

options.label: In the chat
options.caption: In the chat, as the app shows an error from the AI service today.
options.summary: A notice in the chat, where it happened. Stays until your next message, or Dismiss. Try again where the app can retry.
pros: Matches how AI service errors already show.
You can scroll back and see what failed.
cons: Adds a line to the chat.

options.label: Strip, until you act
options.caption: The strip above the message box, as the app shows "Connecting tools…" today.
options.summary: A strip above the box until you type, send, or switch chats.
pros: Hard to miss.
cons: Leaves no trace once gone.

options.label: Floating, timed
options.caption: Floating above the message box, as every notice shows today.
options.summary: As today, with the timer fixed.
pros: Smallest change.
cons: Easy to miss, and no trace afterwards.

steps.checked: Counted and read from the app code on 2026-11-23; every notice is listed under "Every notice, by kind".
steps.caption: A real one, in the app today.

steps.headline: A button didn't work: where should it show, and when should it leave?
steps.today: 39 notices, such as "Couldn't copy — please try again." and "Couldn't save Fast mode.". They float for 3 to 5 seconds.
steps.problem: They are about the whole app, not a chat, so tying them to a chat would be wrong. Today the timer bug can leave them stuck.
steps.proposal: Keep them floating and not tied to a chat, with the timer fixed so they leave after 5 seconds.

options.label: Floating, 5 seconds
options.caption: Floating above the message box, as every notice shows today.
options.summary: Floating above the box, in any chat, leaving after 5 seconds. The timer bug fixed.
pros: Right for a quick "that didn't work".
Nothing else to learn.
cons: Easy to miss if you look away.

options.label: Floating, until closed
options.caption: Floating with a button, as the signed-out notice shows today.
options.summary: Floating until you close it.
pros: Can't be missed.
cons: Small failures pile up as things you have to close.

options.label: Strip in this chat
options.caption: The strip above the message box, as the app shows "Connecting tools…" today.
options.summary: In the strip above whatever chat is open.
pros: One place for everything.
cons: Shows in a chat it has nothing to do with.

steps.checked: Counted and read from the app code on 2026-11-23; every notice is listed under "Every notice, by kind".
steps.caption: A real one, in the app today.

steps.headline: Done: where should a confirmation show, and when should it leave?
steps.today: 3 notices: "Copied to clipboard" and "Saving report.pdf to this device…" and "Voice is ready — tap the mic to talk.". They float for 3 seconds.
steps.problem: Only three things confirm this way; most actions confirm silently or on the button itself.
steps.proposal: Keep them floating for 3 seconds, timer fixed.

options.label: Floating, 3 seconds
options.caption: Floating above the message box, as every notice shows today.
options.summary: As today, with the timer fixed.
pros: Quick and out of the way.
cons: None worth noting.

options.label: On the button
options.summary: Drop the notice; the button itself shows a tick for a moment.
pros: Nothing pops up at all.
cons: "Copied" after typing /copy has no button to show it on.

steps.checked: Counted and read from the app code on 2026-11-23; every notice is listed under "Every notice, by kind".
steps.caption: A real one, in the app today.

steps.headline: Needs you, app-wide: where should it show, and when should it leave?
steps.today: 10 notices, such as "You were signed out of your YouCoded account. Friends see you as offline until you sign in again.". They float for 6 to 30 seconds.
steps.problem: You must do something (sign in, fix a password, check a file), and the notice can vanish before you do.
steps.proposal: Keep them floating in any chat, and keep them until you act or close them.

options.label: Floating, until closed
options.caption: Floating with a button, as the signed-out notice shows today.
options.summary: Floating with its button and a close button. Stays until you act or close it.
pros: Can't be missed.
Not tied to a chat, because it isn't about one.
cons: Covers the bottom of the chat until you deal with it.

options.label: Floating, timed
options.caption: Floating with a button, as the signed-out notice shows today.
options.summary: As today, leaving after 6 to 30 seconds.
pros: Gets out of the way by itself.
cons: Can vanish before you have read it.

steps.intro: Where the notice goes, when it shows, and what happens to your held-back message.

steps.path: The notice above the message box
steps.headline: Now that you have seen every notice: how should they be organized?
steps.today: About 120 short notices share one floating spot above the message box. Most are about one chat; about 45 are about the whole app.
steps.checked: Counted from the app code on 2026-11-23; every one is photographed on the pages before this one.
steps.problem: Notices about one chat float over every chat, and the timer bug can leave any of them on screen while Claude works.
steps.proposal: Pick how they should be organized. Drawings of your pick, made in the real app, come next round.

options.label: Two homes
options.summary: Notices about one chat sit in a strip just above that chat's message box. Notices about the whole app keep floating.
pros: A chat's notice never shows in another chat.
A problem stays until it is fixed; a plain confirmation still leaves after a few seconds.
The strip already exists for "Connecting tools…" and the phone's "Reconnecting…".
cons: Two places to look instead of one.
Each notice has to be sorted into one home or the other.

options.label: All in the strip
options.summary: Every notice, about one chat or the whole app, sits in the strip above the message box.
pros: One place for everything.
Nothing ever covers your messages.
cons: App-wide notices, like a failed download, would sit in whichever chat is open and stay there when you switch.

options.label: Keep floating
options.summary: Everything stays floating as today, with the timer fixed and chat notices shown only in their own chat.
pros: Smallest change; looks the same as today.
cons: Floating notices still cover the bottom of the chat while they show.
Only one can show at a time; a new one replaces the last.

steps.caption: Today, in the real app: a question is waiting and you pressed Send.
steps.resolved: Replaced by one decision per kind of notice, on the first page, with every notice sorted and listed.

steps.path: The notice above the message box
steps.headline: When should the notice appear?
steps.today: Only when you press Send and the message is held back.
steps.checked: Read in the app's code on 2026-11-21.
steps.problem: Claude's question is usually already on screen, so a notice before you send would repeat it.

options.label: After you press Send
options.summary: It only appears when your message is held back, as now.
pros: Never repeats a question you can already see.
Shows exactly when you need to know why nothing sent.
cons: You only learn something is waiting once you try to send.

options.label: Whenever something waits
options.summary: It shows as soon as Claude Code waits on you, even before you type.
pros: You know before you start typing.
cons: Shows on top of a question you can already see, most of the time.

steps.headline: Once you answer, should your held-back message send itself?
steps.today: Your message stays in the box. After answering, you press Send again yourself.
steps.checked: Read in the app's code on 2026-11-21.
steps.problem: Pressing Send twice is a small annoyance; a message sending itself later can be a surprise.

options.label: You press Send again
options.summary: The message waits in the box until you send it.
pros: Nothing sends without you pressing the button.
You can change or delete it first.
cons: One extra press after answering.

options.label: It sends itself
options.summary: The notice says your message will send once you answer, and it goes out as soon as you do.
pros: No second press.
cons: A message typed minutes ago could go out after you changed your mind.
A bigger change to how sending works, so more that could go wrong.

steps.resolved: Kept: you press Send yourself. Your note is the rule: the notice leaves on its own the moment the question is answered.
